name: Earl Sweatshirt
label: Warner Records
lede: A sixteen-year-old MySpace rapper turned Odd Future's darkest weapon, then vanished to Samoa, came back, and spent a decade getting quieter, stranger and better, with a fatherhood album that Pitchfork ranked No. 15 of 2025.

eras.title: Tyler finds a kid on MySpace
eras.text: A Los Angeles teenager rhymes under a joke name, while a few miles of internet away Tyler, the Creator is building a crew that answers to no one. They meet the way 2009 kids did: a message.

years.h: Thebe Kgositsile raps as Sly Tendencies
years.p: Born in Chicago in 1994 and raised in Los Angeles by his mother, the UCLA law professor Cheryl Harris, he starts rapping in seventh grade and posts tracks on MySpace.
years.xp: Wikipedia says he also ran a rap trio, the Backpackerz, with friends Loofy and JW Mijo, which split in 2009. His father was the South African poet Keorapetse Kgositsile; his parents separated when he was six.

years.h: [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]] drops its first tape, three years before anyone cares
years.p: Odd Future Wolf Gang Kill Them All, formed in Los Angeles in 2007 around [[Tyler, the Creator|f6beac20-5dfe-4d1f-ae02-0b0a740aafd6]], [[Hodgy|76600f02-c090-4d15-8782-680cde16bd98]], [[Left Brain|f57d8a69-ed3c-4d18-8bce-0083b162fae6]], [[Casey Veggies|67c6a1f0-7910-4c52-a651-2b7ec819e647]], [[Matt Martians|1018344f-abc8-4c62-b4fd-37a30fd2dc6f]] and [[Syd|7d3d6c65-e053-4657-8705-0ca61bc012ad]], self-releases The Odd Future Tape on November 15.
years.xp: The crew signed with RED Distribution and Sony in April 2011. Its first studio album, The OF Tape Vol. 2, arrived in March 2012, with Earl finally on it.

years.h: Tyler gets a fan message and a new member
years.p: Tyler finds the teenager on MySpace, and Thebe Kgositsile becomes Earl Sweatshirt, a name picked for its old-man sound and a James Pants sweatshirt, and joins Odd Future.

eras.title: Sixteen, notorious, and in Samoa
eras.text: The most talked-about teenage rapper in America drops a mixtape and vanishes. Fans chant for him at shows while he sits in a boarding school on the other side of the Pacific.

years.cap: Earl, free on the Odd Future site, March 31, 2010
years.h: Earl: a 16-year-old's mixtape, free, and unnerving
years.p: Tyler produces most of it; Vince Staples, Hodgy and Syd guest. Pitchfork called it "mesmerizing" and later ranked it among the decade's 100 best albums.
years.xp: Recorded in 2009 and 2010 when Earl was 15 and 16, it was posted as a free download on the Odd Future website. Its graphic, violent narratives were fiction rather than autobiography, per Wikipedia, and reviewers argued over how vile verses could sound so fluent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt · REVOLT: How Earl Sweatshirt grew up
years.h: His mother sends him to a Samoan boarding school
years.p: After the mixtape, Cheryl Harris enrolls him at Coral Reef Academy, a therapeutic school for at-risk boys, where he stays about 18 months. The chant follows Odd Future to every stage.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that behavioral issues and drug use were cited as the reason. At the school he read Manning Marable's Malcolm X biography, and he wrote verses that later ended up on the Odd Future track "Oldie."

REVOLT describes the stay as a turning point: he talked with abuse survivors and worked through his complicated feelings about his father.

years.h: Complex tracks Earl down in Samoa; The New Yorker says he's fine
years.p: Complex confirms in April that he is at Coral Reef Academy; in May Kelefa Sanneh publishes emails in The New Yorker in which Earl says he is not held against his will.
years.xp:
Tyler Craven, an alumnus of the school who had helped Complex find Earl, disputed that account in June, saying on Facebook that the quotes were shaped by staff therapists.

The New Yorker piece also has him asking fans to stop the Free Earl chants. Nobody stopped.

years.cap: Earl Sweatshirt at Day N Night Festival, 2017 · Wikimedia
years.h: Home, and managed by Tupac's old manager
years.p: Leila Steinberg, who once managed Tupac Shakur, brings him back from Samoa in February 2012, and she is still his manager per Wikipedia.

years.h: First album with the crew: The OF Tape Vol. 2
years.p: Earl appears on "Oldie" and joins Odd Future at Hammerstein Ballroom in New York the night the album lands.

years.h: Signs to Columbia, but turns down bigger money
years.p: He gets his own imprint, Tan Cressida, and passes on larger offers to stay close to Odd Future.

years.h: Guests on [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]]'s Channel Orange
years.p: "Super Rich Kids" puts Earl on Ocean's debut album; Wikipedia notes he was nominated for Album of the Year as a featured artist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chum (song) · IMVDb: Hiro Murai on Chum
years.h: "Chum": the comeback, in one take
years.p: The first solo single since Samoa was cut in the first three days of album sessions with [[Christian Rich|e5b5b041-bf22-4658-b58a-8be875674a4c]], vocals in a single take. Pitchfork named it Best New Track.
years.xp:
Director Hiro Murai hung Earl upside down for the performance shots and added the frogs in post. Tyler and his crew turned up mid-shoot riding shopping carts and stormed the set, Murai told IMVDb.

Pitchfork's Larry Fitzmaurice wrote that it was "someone growing into their lyrical talents as they grow up in real time." Wikipedia says it has since gone Gold in the US.

eras.title: Doris and the late-night circuit
eras.text: The debut album arrives with a Billboard top five, a late-night TV spot and a sketch-comedy job. Earl spends it telling everyone he hates the attention.

years.cap: A picture of earl sweatshirt at a festival · Wikimedia
years.src: Stereogum: Tyler, Earl Sweatshirt and Domo Genesis play Letterman
yt: Tyler, Earl and Domo Genesis on Letterman
years.h: Odd Future does "Rusty" on Letterman and takes a selfie
years.p: Tyler, Earl and [[Domo Genesis|0ad99596-cbec-4726-af16-138e2a9268a1]] perform Tyler's "Rusty", hang at the back of the stage, then stalk off before returning to snap a picture with the host.

years.h: Doris: the album about not wanting to be famous
years.p: Recorded from February 2012 to July 2013, with beats from Earl (as randomblackdude), the Neptunes, [[RZA|29c28ac3-27c5-4822-8eb6-0af89a3a7240]] and Christian Rich; debuts at No. 5 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Guests include [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]], [[Vince Staples|78e854b8-9713-4ff2-9218-6b3784893bff]], [[Mac Miller|a0e8a1b1-5f8f-475a-a253-17415c17d0ff]] and Tyler. The Guardian and the Los Angeles Times gave it top marks, per Wikipedia, and Complex ranked it No. 11 on its 2013 albums list.

years.h: Twenty episodes of Loiter Squad
years.p: Earl is a regular on the Adult Swim sketch show Odd Future fronts, running from 2012 to 2014, and performs "Burgundy" with the Roots on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon.

eras.title: Less, on purpose
eras.text: Earl sheds the crew, the label's plan and most of the beats. He puts out an album with no warning and a ten-minute EP on a nameless YouTube account.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside · Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt
years.h: A 30-minute album shows up on iTunes with no announcement
years.p: Earl says the label put it out without notice. He calls it his first real album because he can "back up everything, the good and the bad."
years.xp:
The only Odd Future guest is Vince Staples, alongside Dash, Wiki and Na-Kel Smith. It debuted at No. 12 on the Billboard 200 and Pitchfork ranked it 25th among 2015's albums, per Wikipedia.

Sources differ on the date: the album's Wikipedia page says pre-orders appeared March 17 and it came out March 23, while his artist page says March 16 and March 22.
play: I Don't Like Shit, I Don't Go Outside

years.h: "Solace": ten minutes, dedicated to his mother and grandmother
years.p: Uploaded to a YouTube channel called dar Qness, described by Earl as music from when he "hit the bottom and found something."

years.big: "Thebe and I are fine by the way." Tyler
years.src: DIY: Earl Sweatshirt and Tyler, the Creator comment on Odd Future being over · Wikipedia: Odd Future
years.h: Tyler says Odd Future is over. Then he says it isn't
years.p: Tyler tweets that although it's no more, "those 7 letters are forever"; Earl tweets confirming he is out.
years.xp: Tyler said he had only been looking at old photos and thinking about how time flies, and that one tweet had stirred everything up. The group stayed mostly dormant after 2015, per Wikipedia, and reunited for shows in 2018 and 2023.

years.h: Three SoundCloud tracks, one afternoon's worth
years.p: "Wind in My Sails" (with an Alchemist beat), "Bary" and "Skrt Skrt" drop on SoundCloud on January 25.

eras.title: A father, a new scene, and 15 tracks in 25 minutes
eras.text: Earl moves toward the New York underground and makes his shortest, most private record. His father has died; the samples on it belong to both parents.

years.cap: Tyler The Creator and Earl Sweatshirt performing at the Pomona Fox Theater in 2013. · Wikimedia
years.src: DJBooth: Earl Sweatshirt's Some Rap Songs one year later
years.h: Earl meets the New York crew at XL Recordings
years.p: He gets to know MIKE, Medhane and others from the sLUms scene at XL Recordings in New York and begins showing up in their orbit by 2018.
years.xp: The album sessions started in a home studio in Los Angeles in December 2016 and ran through 2018, per Wikipedia. Producers included Adé Hakim, Black Noi$e, Denmark Vessey and [[Navy Blue|304c731f-ea4f-407c-b4fc-65131b1b2b37]] (Sage Elsesser).

years.src: Wikipedia: Earl Sweatshirt · NPR: Earl Sweatshirt interview transcript
years.h: His father, Keorapetse Kgositsile, dies
years.p: The South African poet lived far from Earl's California childhood; Wikipedia says the relationship was complex and often distant.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the death to January 2018, citing Pitchfork. Earl said the coming album was meant to be themed around his father's death. On NPR he spoke of the frustration of losing his "pops."

years.h: "Nowhere2go": Vince Staples says Earl is back, then he is
years.p: Staples announces on Beats 1 on November 2 that a new Earl album is coming; on November 7 Earl tweets "tap in" and the single appears the next morning.

years.src: Wikipedia: Some Rap Songs · DJBooth: Earl Sweatshirt's Some Rap Songs one year later
years.h: Some Rap Songs: 15 tracks, 25 minutes, one blurry selfie
years.p: Lo-fi, sample-heavy, and closing with "Playing Possum", built on vocal samples of his late father and his mother. It debuts at No. 17 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
The album opens on a James Baldwin sample about imprecise words, and Navy Blue and Standing on the Corner both appear. Metacritic gave it an 86 from 19 reviews, per Wikipedia.

Earl told NPR the title was literal: "swear to God that's some rap songs right there."

years.h: Earl says Some Rap Songs is his last for Columbia
years.p: He tells fans he is excited to be free so he can "do riskier shit."

years.h: Feet of Clay: a 15-minute EP announced the day before
years.p: Warner Records puts it out with beats from The Alchemist, Black Noi$e and Mach-Hommy; a deluxe edition with two bonus tracks follows in July 2020.

eras.title: Free of Columbia: Sick! and a puzzle box
eras.text: Now on Warner and pushing further into rough sound, Earl releases a pandemic-era album and a full album with the Alchemist that arrives through a very online door.

years.h: "2010": the first single in two years
years.p: Earl returns with the single and video for "2010" and follows in December with "Tabula Rasa" featuring Armand Hammer, which announces his fourth album.

years.h: Sick!: ten songs, No. 5 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It peaks at No. 5 on the Billboard 200 and gets an 85 on Metacritic. Guests include Armand Hammer and Zelooperz.
years.xp:
Earl called it his "humble offering of 10 songs recorded in the wake of the worldwide coronavirus pandemic." Production came from Earl, The Alchemist, Black Noi$e, Navy Blue, Samiyam, Theravada and others.

Stereogum's Tom Breihan made it Album of the Week.

years.src: Wikipedia: Voir Dire (Earl Sweatshirt and the Alchemist album)
years.h: Voir Dire with The Alchemist, sold as an NFT
years.p: An album made entirely with [[The Alchemist|03f3deb7-0419-4bf9-a1e7-511946385717]] is announced through a puzzle on a website and released via Gala Music; the NFT tie-in draws backlash.
years.xp: Recorded from late 2020 to 2021, it ended up on streaming services on October 6 with a slightly different tracklist that adds Vince Staples features. Metacritic gave it 83 from nine reviews, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Live Laugh Love
eras.text: A father and married man makes his shortest, weirdest and most tender record, and the year-end critics notice.

years.cap: The Los Angeles listening event, August 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Live Laugh Love (Earl Sweatshirt album)
years.h: An impostor plays Earl's album launch
years.p: The listening event in Los Angeles announces the album without Earl; an Earl Sweatshirt impersonator performs and Black Noi$e DJs from the record.

q: I guess the joke was on me.
years.src: Wikipedia: Live Laugh Love · Metacritic: Live Laugh Love critic reviews · Year-End Lists: Pitchfork
years.h: Live Laugh Love: Pitchfork's 8.5 and No. 15 of 2025
years.p: The 24-minute, 11-track album (Tan Cressida/Warner) is built from Theravada, Black Noi$e, Child Actor and Navy Blue production, and scores an 84 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
Earl told the New York Times Popcast that the title holds both halves of him: "being 16 and then also having a family." Pitchfork's review is listed at 85 on Metacritic, which quotes it: "There's so much musical and personal inspiration colliding at once, you can feel the passion even when you can't quite crack it all."

It peaked at No. 184 on the Billboard 200. Videos followed for "Crisco", "Exhaust" and "Well Done!"

eras.title: Utility
eras.text: The next move is a shared double album with the New York rapper he learned from.

years.h: Double album with MIKE, produced all by Surf Gang
years.p: Mike's Pompeii and Earl's 18-track Utility sit on one release, with sessions in New York and Los Angeles between 2023 and 2025.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.3, per Wikipedia. Utility runs 35 minutes; Mike appears on "Leadbelly".
